A nozzle is positioned within the body and defines an internal cavity configured to direct fuel toward an orifice located at the cavity’s smallest cross-sectional area. Exhaust pressure actuates the piston along the longitudinal axis, thereby controlling the flow of fuel through the nozzle orifice.

outputs.L4:
The recirculation device is configured to combine a metered quantity of fuel with a recirculated exhaust stream. The device includes separate exhaust and fuel passages that communicate with an internal mixing chamber. A nozzle positioned between the fuel passage and the mixing chamber controls the introduction of fuel, while a sliding piston is arranged to move in response to pressure or flow conditions in the exhaust passage. Movement of the piston adjusts the effective flow area through the nozzle, thereby increasing, reducing, or interrupting the supply of fuel to the mixing chamber.

During operation, recirculated exhaust enters the device through the exhaust passage and acts on the piston. The resulting piston displacement regulates fuel flow in accordance with the exhaust conditions. The metered fuel then enters the mixing chamber, where it is combined with the recirculated exhaust before the mixture is discharged for downstream use. By mechanically linking fuel metering to the exhaust stream, the device provides responsive and controlled mixing without requiring the two fluids to share an inlet passage. This arrangement improves regulation of the exhaust-fuel ratio, promotes more uniform mixing, and helps maintain stable operation as exhaust pressure or flow varies.

## The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the most common words in the English language. It is known as the definite article and is used when referring to a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, “the book” points to a particular book rather than any book.

Although “the” is short and simple, it plays an essential role in communication. It helps make sentences precise, natural, and easy to understand. Without it, many English expressions would sound unclear or incomplete.

The word also appears in famous names and titles, such as *The Beatles*, *The Great Gatsby*, and *The New York Times*. Its frequent use demonstrates how even the smallest words can have a significant impact on language.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an exhaust-driven fuel recirculation device with separate exhaust, fuel, and mixture passages, a nozzle, a sliding piston, and an internal mixing chamber.
counterfactuals.output: An exhaust-driven fuel recirculation device includes a housing defining separate exhaust, fuel, and mixture passages. An exhaust nozzle communicates with the exhaust passage and is arranged to direct exhaust gas into an internal mixing chamber. A sliding piston is disposed within the housing and is movable in response to exhaust pressure to selectively regulate communication between the fuel passage and the mixing chamber. Exhaust gas discharged through the nozzle induces and entrains fuel admitted to the mixing chamber, thereby forming an exhaust-fuel mixture. The mixture passage conveys the exhaust-fuel mixture from the mixing chamber for recirculation to an engine intake or other downstream location. The arrangement provides pressure-responsive fuel metering and mixing within a compact device while maintaining separation of the exhaust, fuel, and mixture flow paths upstream of the mixing chamber.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent-oriented description of an exhaust-powered fuel mixing and recirculation device in which a piston moves along the body’s longitudinal axis to meter fuel into a mixing chamber.
counterfactuals.output:
### Exhaust-Powered Fuel Mixing and Recirculation Device

An exhaust-powered fuel conditioning device includes an elongated body defining a longitudinal axis, an exhaust-actuation chamber, a fuel-metering chamber, and a mixing chamber. A piston assembly is disposed within the body for reciprocating movement substantially parallel to the longitudinal axis. The piston assembly includes an exhaust-responsive drive portion and a fuel-metering portion that are mechanically coupled while being fluidly isolated from one another.

An exhaust inlet places the exhaust-actuation chamber in selective fluid communication with an exhaust passage of an internal-combustion engine. Exhaust pressure, including static pressure or pressure pulses produced during engine operation, acts against a drive face of the piston assembly to produce an axial metering stroke. A return member, such as a compression spring, gas spring, opposing exhaust chamber, or magnetic biasing arrangement, urges the piston assembly in an opposite axial direction. An exhaust outlet or pressure-relief passage permits exhaust gas to leave the actuation chamber during the return stroke.

The fuel-metering portion of the piston assembly is received within a metering bore communicating with a fuel inlet and a metered-fuel outlet. Axial displacement of the piston varies the effective volume of the metering chamber and/or the open area of one or more metering ports. Fuel is thereby displaced or admitted in a quantity related to piston travel. An adjustable stop, threaded calibration member, replaceable metering insert, or controllable exhaust valve may be provided to establish the maximum piston stroke and corresponding fuel-delivery quantity.

The metered-fuel outlet opens into the mixing chamber through an injector or atomizing orifice. The mixing chamber further includes a gas inlet configured to receive exhaust gas, intake air, crankcase gas, or a combination thereof. Gas flow through a restricted throat, venturi, swirl passage, or multi-port diffuser promotes atomization and distribution of the metered fuel. The resulting fuel-containing mixture is discharged through a mixture outlet for delivery to an engine intake passage, combustion device, reformer, aftertreatment burner, or other fuel-consuming apparatus.

A recirculation circuit extends from the mixing chamber or mixture outlet to a return inlet positioned upstream of the metering chamber or mixing throat. At least a portion of the fuel-containing mixture is returned through the recirculation circuit to increase residence time, improve vaporization, and reduce localized fuel accumulation. The recirculation circuit may include a separator, check valve, pressure regulator, flow restrictor, cooler, heater, or variable recirculation valve. Separated liquid fuel may be returned to the fuel inlet or to a fuel reservoir, while a gaseous fraction may be reintroduced into the mixing chamber.

In one operating cycle, an exhaust-pressure event enters the exhaust-actuation chamber and advances the piston assembly along the longitudinal axis. Movement of the fuel-metering portion closes the fuel inlet and displaces a defined volume of fuel through the atomizing orifice into the mixing chamber. As exhaust pressure decreases, the return member retracts the piston assembly, reopening the fuel inlet and refilling the metering chamber. Check valves may be arranged at the fuel inlet and metered-fuel outlet to establish unidirectional fuel flow.

The piston assembly may include multiple axially spaced sealing elements and an intermediate vent or drain cavity between the exhaust-responsive portion and the fuel-metering portion. The intermediate cavity prevents exhaust gas from entering the fuel circuit and directs any leakage to a monitored or safely vented location. Thermal barriers, cooling passages, low-conductivity spacers, or heat-resistant coatings may further limit transfer of exhaust heat to the fuel.

Piston stroke may be passively proportional to exhaust pressure or actively regulated. In an actively regulated embodiment, a controller operates an exhaust admission valve, exhaust bypass valve, recirculation valve, or adjustable stroke limiter in response to engine speed, load, exhaust pressure, oxygen concentration, fuel pressure, temperature, or commanded fuel demand. A piston-position sensor may provide feedback indicative of delivered fuel volume.

Accordingly, the device uses energy available in engine exhaust to actuate an axially movable piston, meters fuel without requiring a separate electrically driven pump for each injection event, mixes the metered fuel with a carrier gas, and recirculates at least part of the mixture to improve homogeneity and fuel utilization.
